canonical_question: Does the 'average particle size of less than 10 μm' represent the bulk distribution or just the mean, and could agglomeration affect the SPS densification?

question_variants.question: Does the 'average particle size of less than 10 μm' represent the bulk distribution or just the mean, and could agglomeration affect the SPS densification?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper states that the equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi HEA powders after 40 h of milling had an 'average particle size of less than 10 μm'. It does not provide the full distribution data or explicitly discuss the effect of agglomeration on SPS densification, though the bulk density measurement (96.75% relative density) suggests good densification.

answers.answer: The text reports that the equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi HEA powders after 40 h of milling had an average particle size of less than 10 μm. The resulting bulk density was 10.6 g/cm^3 with a relative density of 96.75% after SPS, but the specific nature of the distribution (bulk vs mean) and agglomeration effects are not detailed.
answers.measurement_outcome: Average particle size < 10 μm, Relative density 96.75%
answers.boundary_limitation: Distribution details and agglomeration effects not specified
evidence_spans: Figure 1 a shows the XRD patterns of the equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi high entropy alloy powders with different milling times.
Subsequently, two overlapping peaks near the peaks of W and Mo, characterized as body-centered cubic (BCC) solutions, are observed in the XRD pattern after 20 h.

It can be hypothesized that the solid solution sequence of the elements is related to the melting point, with low-melting-point elements being dissolved more quickly than the elements with higher melting points, which has been similarly reported in the previous work [ [18] ].
